archived_tasks.title: Hotspot walk batch 3 (functions 31-50)
archived_tasks.description: Review: Wishlist/Send, ConfigurableProduct/CartItemProcessor, Eav/AbstractEntity, Tax/Calculation, Catalog/Option/File, Sales/Email/Sender, Cms/FilterProvider, ImportExport/Import, Backup, OauthService, Swagger, UrlRewrite/DbStorage, Customer/FileProcessor, Currency, Captcha, Persistent/Session, Csp/Collector, Variable, Widget/Filter, Theme/Design.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Hotspot walk batch 3: Reviewed Wishlist/Send, OauthService, Swagger/Schema, Backup/Rollback FTP, Variable, UrlRewrite, Widget/Filter, Customer/FileProcessor. Found 3 new findings: L-049 (OAuth token secrets asymmetric encryption), G-025 (unauthenticated API schema endpoint), L-050 (backup rollback FTP SSRF). Dismissed OAuth nonce race condition (DB PRIMARY KEY constraint). Multiple areas already covered by existing findings.

archived_tasks.title: Validate H-001: SQL injection in setup DbValidator
archived_tasks.description: H-001 is the only unvalidated HIGH finding. DbValidator::checkDatabasePrivileges() interpolates $dbName into SQL at lines 145,196-197. Validate: (1) Confirm the injection is real by reading source. (2) Check if setup mode restricts access (setup wizard only accessible pre-install or after env.php deletion). (3) Assess if the setup wizard is typically web-accessible in production. (4) If exploitable, write PoC curl command. (5) Set validation_status to confirmed or downgraded.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Validated H-001: SQL injection in DbValidator confirmed as real but downgraded from HIGH to LOW. The injection exists at lines 145 and 196-197, but the only entry points are CLI commands requiring server shell access. The web setup wizard has been removed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate stored XSS chain: M-010 (weak XSS filter) + L-005 (CSP disabled)
archived_tasks.description: M-010 shows REST API XSS filter only blocks script tags. L-005 shows CSP is in report-only mode. Together, this creates a stored XSS path. Trace: (1) Which anonymous API endpoints accept user data rendered in admin HTML? (2) Verify img onerror, svg onload, event handlers pass the filter. (3) Check if output encoding (escapeHtml) catches what the filter misses. (4) If any rendering path lacks encoding, this is a HIGH stored XSS. Combines task_099 and task_102 scopes.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated M-010+L-005 stored XSS chain. Output encoding mitigates all verified rendering paths. M-010 downgraded to LOW.

archived_tasks.title: Chain investigation: Admin SSRF (G-012) -> Redis session injection (G-011) -> RCE
archived_tasks.description: G-012 (ES TestConnection SSRF) allows admin to make requests to arbitrary hosts. G-011 (session deser) shows PHP session handler doesnt restrict object classes. Chain: admin uses TestConnection to scan for Redis on internal network, then uses SSRF or direct Redis access to inject serialized PHP objects into session store. Verify: (1) Can TestConnection reach Redis port 6379? (2) Does response leak enough info to confirm Redis? (3) Can Redis RESP protocol be spoken through HTTP SSRF? (4) What __destruct gadgets are available?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Chain investigation: Admin SSRF (G-012) -> Redis session injection (G-011) -> RCE is NOT exploitable as a single chain. HTTP SSRF via Elasticsearch TestConnection uses Guzzle 7/cURL which blocks CRLF injection in URLs, preventing Redis RESP protocol injection. Non-HTTP schemes (gopher://) blocked by buildESConfig URL construction. SSRF provides service discovery only. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate HTTP cron trigger security
archived_tasks.description: pub/cron.php accepts HTTP GET params via escapeshellarg. Check auth, .htaccess blocking, and param influence on cron execution.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed pub/cron.php has no application-level authentication - relies entirely on web server config (.htaccess and nginx.conf.sample both block it). GET parameters control cron group execution. Exception output discloses full stack traces. Shell injection prevented by double escapeshellarg(). Rated LOW due to web server mitigations. Recorded as L-051.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate AdminNotification feed SSRF/XXE
archived_tasks.description: AdminNotification/Model/Feed.php fetches XML from configurable feed URL. Check if admin-configurable (SSRF), XML parsing safety (XXE), and data handling.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigation of AdminNotification Feed SSRF/XXE found no new vulnerabilities beyond existing findings. Feed URL is hardcoded in config.xml and NOT exposed in system.xml, so admin cannot change it via UI or config save API (filterNodes validates against system.xml paths). SimpleXMLElement without LIBXML_NOENT is safe in PHP 8.x (entity expansion disabled by default - verified via snippet test). Feed data is escaped via escapeHtml() before DB storage. Existing L-002 covers the XXE defense-in-depth concern. AR-5 risk confirmed: feed URL is NOT admin-configurable, SSRF risk negligible.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate LoginAsCustomer authentication security
archived_tasks.description: LoginAsCustomer uses secret-based auth with configurable expiry. Check secret generation (CSPRNG?), one-time-use, ACL requirements, audit logging, and invalidation.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Deep investigation of LoginAsCustomer authentication security. Confirmed existing findings M-027 (GraphQL consent bypass + no audit logging) and L-042 (secret via GET URL). The encrypted-secret authentication mechanism uses ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption with a hardcoded 10-second lifetime, which is reasonably secure. Key observations: (1) The URL secret is NOT one-time-use but 10s window makes replay impractical. (2) Session management is sound: regeneration, persistent cookie cleanup, admin logout invalidation. (3) ACL enforcement proper. (4) configurable authentication_data_expiration_time is dead code. (5) roleHasResource misleading name but correct logic. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Trace FormData parse_str parameter injection in admin attribute save
archived_tasks.description: FormData::unserialize() uses parse_str() + array_replace_recursive() enabling parameter injection via URL-encoded bracket notation. Find ALL callers, check if parse_str can inject unexpected keys that alter model behavior or overwrite protected fields.
archived_tasks.result_summary: FormData::unserialize() parse_str parameter injection trace - SAFE. Both callers are admin-only controllers requiring Magento_Catalog::attributes_attributes ACL. parse_str uses safe two-argument form. serialized_options can override POST keys but admin already controls POST body. No finding warranted.

archived_tasks.title: Trace CatalogUrlRewrite column name injection in SQL WHERE
archived_tasks.description: CatalogUrlRewrite DbStorage::prepareSelect() concatenates column names directly without quoteIdentifier() (parent class uses it). Trace all callers to determine if URL routing passes user-controlled data as array keys that become column names in SQL.
archived_tasks.result_summary: CatalogUrlRewrite DbStorage and DynamicStorage prepareSelect() concatenate column names without quoteIdentifier(), but all callers pass hardcoded string constants as array keys. No user-controlled data flows into column name position. Values are properly parameterized. Defense-in-depth inconsistency but not exploitable. Flow marked safe.

archived_tasks.title: Trace MediaGalleryUi REGEXP pattern injection in directory filter
archived_tasks.description: MediaGalleryUi Directory filter concatenates user path value into MySQL REGEXP pattern. Only % is stripped; regex metacharacters (.*+()[]|) are NOT stripped. Check if this is admin-only, whether ReDoS or directory enumeration is possible.
archived_tasks.result_summary: MediaGalleryUi Directory REGEXP pattern injection is safe. SQL injection prevented by parameterized query (?). Regex metachar injection is possible but admin-only (Magento_Cms::media_gallery ACL), MySQL REGEXP engine is ReDoS-resistant (DFA/ICU), and admin already has full directory browsing access. No finding warranted.

archived_tasks.title: Trace XML Layout simplexml_load_string for XXE in admin layout XML
archived_tasks.description: Framework View Layout and Merge classes use simplexml_load_string without LIBXML_NONET/LIBXML_NOENT protection. Check if admin-supplied layout XML (custom widgets, CMS pages) reaches these calls. Also check DOMDocument LIBXML_PARSEHUGE usage for billion laughs DoS.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Traced simplexml_load_string and DOMDocument XML parsing in Framework View Layout. All calls are safe from XXE on PHP 8.3+ (external entity loading disabled by default, no LIBXML_NOENT flag used). Internal entity expansion (billion laughs) is blocked because user-controlled layout XML (CMS pages) is wrapped inside <layout> element tags before parsing, making DTD declarations syntactically invalid. LIBXML_PARSEHUGE in Xhtml/Template only processes filesystem template files. No finding warranted.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate CSRF bypass via XHR exemption in CsrfValidator
archived_tasks.description: CsrfValidator skips CSRF validation for XHR/AJAX requests (line 75 isAjax check). Investigate: (1) How is isAjax determined? X-Requested-With header? (2) Can attacker set this header cross-origin to bypass CSRF? (3) What state-changing POST endpoints accept AJAX and could be CSRF-attacked? (4) Check if SameSite=Lax cookie provides sufficient protection for same-site but cross-origin scenarios.
archived_tasks.result_summary: CSRF XHR bypass in CsrfValidator is NOT exploitable. The isXmlHttpRequest() check relies on X-Requested-With header which triggers CORS preflight for cross-origin requests. Magento has no CORS configuration, so browsers block cross-origin XHR with custom headers. SameSite=Lax on session cookies provides additional protection. Admin BackendValidator does NOT have the XHR bypass. Dismissed as non-finding.

archived_tasks.title: Audit Knockout html: binding templates for attacker-reachable data sources
archived_tasks.description: G-009 documented 25+ KO templates using html: binding. For each: (1) Trace the data source — is it admin-only or could a customer/anonymous user control it? (2) Check if backend escaping is actually applied before the data reaches window.checkoutConfig or AJAX responses. Focus on: checkoutConfig.payment.instructions, cart().subtotal, product_name in minicart, option.value, checkboxText in agreements, shippingPolicyContent. Any customer-controllable data rendered via html: without encoding is stored XSS.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Validated all KO html: binding data sources. Backend escaping consistently applied for core paths. No customer-reachable XSS in core. additional_options path bypasses escapeHtml. G-009 validated as informational.

archived_tasks.title: Cart item modification race during checkout (CartMutex vs QuoteMutex divergence)
archived_tasks.description: CartMutex (LockManager) protects placeOrder while QuoteMutex (SELECT FOR UPDATE) protects item saves. These different lock mechanisms don't synchronize. Verify: 1) Can a concurrent item save change cart contents while placeOrder runs? 2) Does submitQuote recalculate totals or trust cached values? 3) Does the payment gateway verify authorized amount matches capture amount? 4) Check all GraphQL/REST endpoints that modify cart items for QuoteMutex usage.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated CartMutex vs QuoteMutex divergence in checkout flow. Confirmed placeOrder loads fresh quote after lock, calls collectTotals via importData - no price manipulation via race. Found UpdateCartItems, RemoveItemFromCart, ApplyCouponToCart, RemoveCouponFromCart have NO mutex at all (L-052). Updated L-015 with details confirming low severity.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate full email enumeration -> credential attack chain
archived_tasks.description: Chain: M-005 + M-006 + G-006 + G-008 provide email enumeration. H-004 + M-011 provide unthrottled auth endpoints. Verify the end-to-end chain: (1) Enumerate emails via isEmailAvailable (no rate limit). (2) Detect locked accounts via G-006. (3) Brute-force passwords via admin/customer token endpoints. (4) Assess combined severity. Subsumes task_042 scope.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated the full email enumeration to credential brute-force chain. Confirmed end-to-end unauthenticated attack: (1) isEmailAvailable endpoint has zero rate limiting/CAPTCHA, (2) token endpoints have per-username-only lockout (6/10 failures) with no per-IP limiting, (3) distributed attack across N enumerated emails yields N*5 guesses per 30min from single IP. Recorded H-006 as HIGH chain finding combining 13 individual findings.

archived_tasks.title: Chain: IP spoofing (M-018) bypasses per-IP CAPTCHA threshold (M-022/M-023)
archived_tasks.description: M-018 shows RemoteAddress trusts X-Forwarded-For without proxy validation. M-022/M-023 show CAPTCHA per-IP threshold is 1000 (effectively no limit). Chain: attacker spoofs X-Forwarded-For to rotate IPs, making per-IP CAPTCHA/rate limiting completely ineffective. Verify: (1) Does X-Forwarded-For spoofing actually reset the per-IP CAPTCHA counter? (2) Does it also bypass RequestThrottler per-IP tracking? (3) What is the combined impact on brute-force protection for admin and customer logins? If confirmed, this upgrades M-022+M-023 severity.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed chain: M-018 (X-Forwarded-For IP spoofing) completely bypasses M-022 (CAPTCHA per-IP threshold) and Backpressure rate limiting (IdentityProvider). All three mechanisms use RemoteAddress::getRemoteAddress() which trusts X-Forwarded-For with no trustedProxies. Rotating the header gives fresh counters per request. Recorded as H-007 (high severity chain). RequestThrottler is per-account only (not IP-based) so it is not directly bypassed but cannot prevent cross-account credential stuffing.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate user content features (review XSS, contact injection, wishlist IDOR)
archived_tasks.description: Multiple features accept user content. Investigate: (1) Review XSS. (2) Contact form email header injection. (3) SendFriend email injection. (4) Wishlist sharing token predictability. (5) Wishlist IDOR. (6) Rate limiting on reviews/contact/sendfriend.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated user content features (Review, Contact, SendFriend, Wishlist sharing). Most areas already covered by existing findings (L-030, L-034, L-037, G-017, G-022). Found new informational finding G-026: Shared Wishlist Cart controller loads any wishlist item by ID without verifying it belongs to a shared wishlist. Reviews use escapeHtml() properly in all templates. Wishlist sharing codes use CSPRNG (~190 bits entropy).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate downloadable product link security and product alert
archived_tasks.description: Downloadable products serve files to customers. Investigate: (1) Download link auth bypass. (2) Path traversal in file serving (LFI). (3) Sample download without auth. (4) Download link token security. (5) ProductAlert unsubscribe CSRF.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated downloadable product link security and ProductAlert unsubscribe. Found 2 new issues: L-053 (predictable link hash) and L-054 (download counter race condition).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate admin backup download security and encryption key management
archived_tasks.description: Backup module creates full DB/filesystem backups. Investigate: (1) Backup download path traversal. (2) Backup file web-accessible? (3) Backup ACL scope. (4) Encryption key rotation. (5) Rollback to insecure state.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated admin backup download security and encryption key management. Found 2 new findings: (G-027) Database/system backups store complete unencrypted sensitive data dumps in var/backups/; (L-055) Backup download lacks step-up auth while rollback requires it. Existing findings M-003, L-044, L-050 already covered other aspects. Module disabled by default. Name param sanitized. Type validated. Path traversal mitigated.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate multishipping checkout step-skipping and InstantPurchase token security
archived_tasks.description: Multishipping has 30 controllers with complex state transitions. Investigate: (1) Step skipping. (2) State manipulation between steps. (3) Address IDOR. (4) InstantPurchase token replay/CSRF. (5) Race conditions.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated multishipping checkout step-skipping and InstantPurchase token/address security. Found M-029: InstantPurchase Address IDOR where authenticated customer can use any other customer address for instant purchase orders (missing ownership check in InstantPurchaseOptionLoadingFactory::getAddress()). Found G-028: Multishipping Overview/OverviewPost controllers skip step-completion validation (informational). Multishipping address handling correctly protected via isAddressIdApplicable(). createOrders uses cartMutex.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate catalog search injection and coupon code brute-force
archived_tasks.description: Search is unauthenticated and reaches Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Investigate: (1) Search query injection. (2) Search DoS. (3) Advanced search SQL injection. (4) Coupon brute-force rate limiting. (5) Coupon code timing enumeration.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated catalog search injection and coupon code security. Found: (1) Elasticsearch wildcard query injection via Advanced Search SKU field (L-056). (2) Coupon brute-force feasible via GraphQL with 1000 attempts per IP (L-057). Dismissed: main search match query injection (not exploitable), advanced search SQL injection (whitelisted), coupon timing oracle (no meaningful differential).

archived_tasks.title: Verify Customer Address File Upload auth bypass (M-017)
archived_tasks.description: Confirm that Customer/Controller/Address/File/Upload.php is reachable without customer session. Verify: (1) Does CSRF validation apply? (2) Does the CMS/middleware add any other auth check? (3) Test with non-existent attribute code. (4) Check if similar gap exists in Customer/Controller/File/Upload (customer file, not address). (5) Check other Customer controllers extending Action without AccountInterface.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed M-017: Customer Address File Upload (Address/File/Upload.php) is accessible without customer authentication. Controller extends Action (not AccountInterface), so the auth plugin does not intercept. CSRF bypassed via XMLHttpRequest header. Requires admin-configured file-type address attribute (non-default). NotProtectedExtension denylist applies but non-image files get no content validation. No parallel customer-level file upload controller exists on frontend. This is the only Customer frontend controller extending Action without AccountInterface.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Redis session/cache authentication defaults and deserialization exposure
archived_tasks.description: Redis defaults to no authentication in Magento setup. Check: (1) Default Redis config for sessions and cache - is auth enforced? (2) If Redis is unauthenticated, can an attacker write to session store to trigger PHP native session deserialization (bypasses allowed_classes=false)? (3) Can cache poisoning via unauthenticated Redis manipulate system config data? (4) Check if Cm\RedisSession uses compression that would complicate exploitation. Related: G-011.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed Redis session deserialization RCE chain (G-011 upgraded to medium with full technical verification). Compression bypass verified: _decodeData() passes through uncompressed data unchanged. PHP session engine deserializes without allowed_classes=false, bypassing Magento safe Serialize.php. New finding M-030: ACL cache poisoning via unauthenticated Redis enables admin privilege escalation (ACL cache NOT encrypted unlike system config cache). Docker compose exposes Redis on 0.0.0.0:6379 without authentication.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate all consumers of RemoteAddress for IP spoofing impact
archived_tasks.description: RemoteAddress trusts X-Forwarded-For without proxy validation (M-018). Enumerate all PHP classes that inject/use RemoteAddress to determine the full blast radius. Key consumers: CAPTCHA rate limiting, RequestThrottler, admin session validation, order fraud detection, logging. Check if any consumer independently validates the IP or if all are vulnerable.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Enumerated all 15 PHP files consuming RemoteAddress and mapped 10 distinct security-relevant impacts. Updated M-018 with comprehensive blast radius. No new high/critical findings beyond what H-007 already covers. Key additional impacts: maintenance mode IP allowlist bypass, developer IP allowlist bypass, password reset rate limiting bypass, SendFriend email rate limiting bypass, backpressure identity spoofing for guests, audit log poisoning.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate OAuth 1.0a implementation security
archived_tasks.description: Review Magento OAuth 1.0a implementation for: (1) Token generation entropy in Oauth/Token.php. (2) Signature validation in Framework/Oauth/Oauth.php (already uses Security::compareStrings). (3) Consumer secret storage and rotation. (4) Token expiration and revocation completeness. (5) OAuth callback URL validation - is redirect_uri validated against registered callback? (6) Check for token fixation or replay attacks. Files: Integration/Model/Oauth/*, Framework/Oauth/*, Integration/etc/webapi.xml
archived_tasks.result_summary: OAuth 1.0a implementation is well-secured. Token generation uses CSPRNG (random_int) with 165-bit entropy. Signature validation enforces HMAC-SHA256 only with timing-safe comparison (Security::compareStrings). Verifier validation also uses timing-safe comparison. Nonce replay protection via DB-stored nonces with composite primary key and 600s timestamp tolerance. Consumer secrets encrypted in DB. Request throttling enforces 6 failures max with 30-minute lockout. No new findings - existing L-049 (unencrypted request/verifier token secrets) already captures the main concern.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate DownloadCustomOption secret key IDOR
archived_tasks.description: Sales/Controller/Download/DownloadCustomOption.php:107 uses loose comparison (!=) for secret_key validation. Also NO customer session check. Investigate: (1) How is secret_key generated - entropy? (2) Can quote_item_option IDs be enumerated? (3) Does the loose != comparison allow bypass on PHP 8.3+? (4) Is there any auth check preventing anonymous download if ID+key known? (5) What files can be downloaded via this endpoint?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated DownloadCustomOption secret key IDOR across Sales and Wishlist controllers. Secret key is substr(sha256(file_contents), 0, 20) = 80 bits entropy - strong against brute force. Loose comparison near-impossible to exploit with hex output on PHP 8.3+. Sales controller has no auth (already G-020). Wishlist controller requires customer auth but has no ownership check on wishlist item option (defense-in-depth gap). All issues already captured in L-009, L-011, G-020. No new findings needed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate guest order lookup brute-force potential
archived_tasks.description: Guest order viewing (Sales/Helper/Guest.php) requires order_id + billing_lastname + (email OR zip). No rate limiting or CAPTCHA observed on this lookup. Investigate: (1) Is there rate limiting on /sales/guest/view? (2) How predictable are order increment IDs? (3) Can lastname+zip be brute-forced for known order IDs? (4) The protectCode in cookie - how is it generated and how long is it? (5) Can the cookie-based access persist indefinitely?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated guest order lookup brute-force potential. Confirmed L-036 findings about no CAPTCHA/rate limiting. Discovered inconsistency: web form (Guest.php) allows looking up registered customer orders, while GraphQL (GuestOrder.php) correctly blocks them via getCustomerId() check. Protect code is strong (32-hex SHA256 of CSPRNG, not brute-forceable). Cookie lifetime 600s with timing-safe hash_equals. New finding L-058 for the missing customerId check on web form path.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate StompClient Jolokia credential exposure and all TLS disable patterns
archived_tasks.description: M-012: StompClient sends ActiveMQ credentials over HTTP without TLS verification. Investigate: (1) All other curl usage in codebase for similar CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=false patterns. (2) Impact of Jolokia access - can attacker execute JMX operations? (3) Is the Jolokia URL configurable or hardcoded? (4) Are there other places where internal service credentials are transmitted insecurely?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed M-012 (StompClient Jolokia TLS disable) with deeper analysis. Found new L-059: retryConnection() hardcodes tcp:// causing silent TLS downgrade when SSL is configured. Verified StompClient is the ONLY hardcoded TLS disable in the codebase. Jolokia provides full JMX management. No JMX mbean injection risk.

archived_tasks.title: Deep-dive coupon/rule per-customer usage race condition
archived_tasks.description: M-014: TOCTOU between Utility::canProcessRule() and Processor::updateCustomerRuleUsages(). Investigate: (1) Async coupon usage publisher races. (2) LockManager implementation. (3) CouponUsagesDecrement abuse. (4) lockLoadedCoupon effectiveness. (5) Guest user exploitation.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Deep investigation of coupon/rule per-customer usage race conditions. Confirmed M-014 and M-016 with deeper technical evidence across 3 unlocked TOCTOU windows. Discovered 2 new findings: L-060 (lockLoadedCoupon silently skips on lock failure) and L-061 (guest checkout bypasses per-customer coupon limits).

archived_tasks.title: Verify JS escaper data: URI bypass is exploitable via any code path
archived_tasks.description: L-014 found JS escaper.js _checkHrefValue only blocks javascript: URIs, not data: URIs. The PHP Escaper blocks both. Verify: (1) Which code paths use JS escaper as sole defense (not backend-escaped)? (2) Can product names or messages contain <a> tags that reach JS escaper with allowedTags including a? (3) Test if data:text/html href passes the escaper in a real browser. (4) Check if any non-anchor element attributes could be used for XSS via the allowed style attribute.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Validated L-014 JS escaper data: URI bypass. Confirmed the technical gap: _checkHrefValue only blocks javascript: URIs, allowing data:, vbscript:, and all other dangerous protocols through. Four components use allowedTags with a: product/name.js, Theme/messages.js, MediaGalleryUi/grid/messages.js, Ui/grid/cells/sanitizedHtml.js. However, no practical exploitation path exists: (1) all content is admin-controlled or hardcoded server messages, (2) modern browsers block data: URI navigation from <a> tags, (3) mage-messages cookie is SameSite=Strict. Also identified style attribute CSS value sanitization asymmetry between PHP and JS escapers. LOW severity confirmed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate symlink handling in Magento file operations
archived_tasks.description: Framework Filesystem Driver File.php uses symlink() and is_link(). Investigate: (1) Are symlinks followed when reading uploaded files? (2) Can symlink be created via archive extraction (TAR/ZIP)? (3) Does PathValidator resolve symlinks before comparison? (4) Can media sync or image resize follow symlinks to read sensitive files?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated symlink handling in Magento file operations. Found L-062 (TAR symlink extraction without target validation) and G-029 (PathValidator getRealPathSafety does not resolve symlinks). Both admin-only but structural defense-in-depth gaps.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Host header usage in SOAP/REST schema URLs and email links
archived_tasks.description: getHttpHost() is used in: Webapi SOAP server (Soap.php:131), REST schema request processor (SchemaRequestProcessor.php:58), WebapiAsync schema (AsynchronousSchemaRequestProcessor.php:77), and PageCache Server (Server.php:70). Verify whether these Host header uses can poison WSDL URLs, REST schema discovery, or password reset links. Check if BaseUrlChecker.php enforcement is applied before these uses.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated Host header usage in SOAP/REST schema endpoints and PageCache Server. Found REST Swagger schema endpoints embed unvalidated Host header in Swagger JSON host field with cache poisoning vector (L-063). BaseUrlChecker not applied to webapi areas. SOAP WSDL safe. PageCache already covered by L-019.

archived_tasks.title: Verify API token revocation completeness across all credential change paths
archived_tasks.description: M-021 found that password change/reset do not revoke API tokens. Investigate ALL credential change paths (password change, password reset, email change, admin forced reset, account deactivation) and verify which ones revoke tokens. Check both opaque tokens (Integration module) and JWT tokens (JwtUserToken module). Verify SessionCleaner also invalidates JWT token claims. Check if there is any token expiry mechanism that limits the window.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Verified M-021 (customer tokens not revoked on password change/reset) and L-025 (email change observer area gap). Discovered L-064: Admin API tokens also not revoked on admin password change or reset. Token revocation only occurs on: explicit manual revocation, account deactivation, account deletion, email change (webapi_rest/graphql only). Password changes/resets for both customer and admin never revoke tokens.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate path traversal in customer file view controllers
archived_tasks.description: Admin Viewfile controllers (Customer/Controller/Adminhtml/Index/Viewfile.php and Address/Viewfile.php) serve files from media directory based on URL-decoded user input. Check: (1) mb_strpos check for .. is sufficient (no encoding bypasses?), (2) URL decoder output is safe, (3) No symlink following. Also check if there are any frontend (non-admin) controllers that serve customer files.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated Customer Viewfile controllers for path traversal. Both admin-only with ACL. Path traversal prevented by mb_strpos dotdot check + PathValidator containment + isFile check. Base64-decoded input prefixed with customer/ or customer_address/. No frontend Viewfile controllers. No bypass found. No new finding.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate crypt/key exposure vectors (chains with JWT key L-016)
archived_tasks.description: crypt/key is the master secret for JWT signing, encryption, and password hashing. Investigate all vectors that could expose env.php or crypt/key: 1) Error messages that include config paths 2) Debug/developer mode info disclosure 3) Backup files in web root (env.php.bak, etc) 4) phpinfo() exposure 5) SSRF to internal config endpoints 6) DeploymentConfig read access from any frontend/API controller. This chains with L-016 (JWT key derived from crypt/key).
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated crypt/key exposure vectors. Found developer mode stack trace exposure, error report files, MAGE_DEBUG_SHOW_ARGS partial secret leakage, and MAGENTO_DC__OVERRIDE env var injection. Crypt/key is well-protected by default. Filed L-065 and G-030.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate file content-type validation gaps in upload paths
archived_tasks.description: Multiple upload endpoints check file extensions but not file content magic bytes. Investigate: (1) Can polyglot files bypass extension checks (e.g., GIF89a + PHP content)? (2) Do image processing functions (GD2) reject non-image content? (3) Is Content-Type from upload trusted vs actual file type? (4) Does X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff protect against MIME sniffing for served files?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated file content-type validation gaps across all upload paths. Image uploads use getimagesize()/GD2 for magic byte validation. Non-image uploads use extension-only validation. Polyglot files (GIF89a+PHP) pass validation but cannot execute due to multi-layer web server protections. MediaStorage Image Validator defaults to valid=true for non-image content (G-031 informational). No exploitable content-type bypass found.

archived_tasks.title: Verify system config cache uses encryption + native Serialize - assess cache poisoning impact
archived_tasks.description: Config/App/Config/Type/System.php uses native PHP Serialize (via di.xml override) for system config cache, but data is encrypted with encryptor before caching. Verify: (1) Is encryption applied on ALL cache write paths? (2) If an attacker has the encryption key (env.php), can they craft a valid encrypted+serialized payload? (3) What security-critical config values pass through this path (admin URLs, allowed IPs, auth settings)? (4) Even with allowed_classes=false, can array/primitive injection change security posture?
archived_tasks.result_summary: System config cache well-defended. All write paths use ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encryption. allowed_classes=false prevents RCE. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Elasticsearch/OpenSearch TestConnection SSRF (G-012)
archived_tasks.description: TestConnection.php:80 passes all request params to clientResolver->create() which builds arbitrary HTTP connection. Investigate: (1) Can admin with catalog config ACL reach this? (2) Is there any response data returned to admin that reveals internal service info? (3) Can the enableAuth flag embed credentials in URL to exfiltrate to attacker host? (4) Check OpenSearch variant at OpenSearch/Block/Adminhtml/System/Config/TestConnection.php. (5) Check if error messages leak connection details.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed G-012 SSRF finding with additional credential exfiltration and error message leakage vectors. Both Elasticsearch8 and OpenSearch variants use identical URL construction that embeds admin-configured credentials in URLs to attacker-controlled hosts. Error messages leak internal network details. Finding updated with validation_status=confirmed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Varnish ban() regex injection via X-Magento-Tags-Pattern
archived_tasks.description: The Varnish VCL uses ban('obj.http.X-Magento-Tags ~ ' + req.http.X-Magento-Tags-Pattern) directly from the request header. While PURGE requests are restricted to the ACL, investigate: (1) Whether a compromised/internal host in the ACL can inject malicious regex patterns that cause ReDoS in Varnish ban processing, (2) Whether the tag pattern from PurgeCache is sanitized before being sent as header value, (3) Whether CRLF in the tag pattern could inject additional headers in the PURGE request.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigation dismissed - no exploitable finding. Varnish ban() regex injection requires ACL membership (PURGE method restricted to configured IPs). Cache tags originate from model getIdentities() using constant+integer_id patterns. No user-controlled content reaches tag values. CRLF injection blocked by Laminas HTTP header validation.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate error report file access and information disclosure
archived_tasks.description: Error reports are stored in var/report/ with 64-char hex IDs. Investigate: (1) What data is stored in report files (exception messages may contain SQL queries, file paths, credentials), (2) Report ID validation uses /^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/ - is this sufficient entropy to prevent brute-force enumeration? (3) Are report files accessible via web when var/ is exposed? (4) Can MAGE_DEBUG_SHOW_ARGS env var expose function arguments (including passwords) in error reports?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated error report information disclosure. Validated existing findings G-030 and L-065. Enhanced G-030 with additional context: MAGE_DEBUG_SHOW_ARGS affects production report storage (not just dev mode), .htaccess.sample enables it by default, sendReport emails full traces via unencrypted mail(), report directories created with 0777 permissions, and report ID shown to all users on error pages. No new standalone finding needed.

archived_tasks.title: DI plugin/interceptor security bypass
archived_tasks.description: 286 plugins, 127 di.xml. Investigate plugins on auth methods, CSRF bypass via CsrfValidator plugins, input mod after sanitization, ACL bypass, plugin sort order windows.
archived_tasks.result_summary: DI plugin/interceptor security investigation completed. No auth bypass, CSRF bypass, or ACL bypass vulnerabilities found in first-party plugins. Interceptor system is architecturally sound. UI Render/Export ACL bypass already covered by M-028.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate what sensitive data is stored with legacy ciphers and re-encryption gaps
archived_tasks.description: Determine what types of sensitive data may still be encrypted with legacy Blowfish-ECB or Rijndael-128-ECB in production databases. Check if there is any re-encryption mechanism when keys are rotated. Examine the encryptData/decryptData patterns in the codebase to understand which database fields contain encrypted values. Check if payment/credential data could still be ECB-encrypted.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated legacy encrypted data persistence and re-encryption coverage gaps. Found that key rotation re-encryption (encryption:data:re-encrypt) only covers core_config_data and sales_order_payment.cc_number_enc, while OAuth access token secrets and consumer secrets have no re-encryptor registered. After key rotation, these sensitive values remain encrypted with the old key indefinitely. Recorded as L-066.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate weak PRNG usage in security-sensitive contexts beyond cache cookies
archived_tasks.description: Audit all uses of rand(), mt_rand(), uniqid() that may be security-relevant. Focus on: (1) MessageQueue correlation_id using rand() - can this enable message hijacking? (2) uniqid() in lock cache signing - can this enable lock bypass? (3) Any other non-CSPRNG usage generating tokens, nonces, or security-relevant values. The framework Math/Random class correctly uses random_int() but many places bypass it.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated all weak PRNG (rand/mt_rand/uniqid) usage in security contexts. Found: (1) MessageQueue RPC correlation_id uses rand() with ~31-bit space - informational since requires AMQP broker access (G-032). (2) Lock Cache signing uses random_bytes(4) primary with uniqid fallback - safe in practice. (3) Message IDs use uniqid for deduplication - not security-relevant. (4) All other uniqid/rand uses are for HTML IDs, temp filenames, or UI elements. No new high/medium findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate email enumeration via isEmailAvailable API
archived_tasks.description: (SUBSUMED by task_107) POST /V1/customers/isEmailAvailable is anonymous. Check if it can enumerate registered emails. Also check password reset endpoint for similar enumeration. Check GraphQL equivalent. [SUBSUMED by completed task_107 scope]
archived_tasks.result_summary: Task fully subsumed by completed task_107 (investigate:email_enumeration_chain). All email enumeration vectors already covered by findings M-005, M-006, G-008, and H-006. No additional investigation needed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Swagger API documentation exposure in production
archived_tasks.description: Swagger module serves API docs. Check: is it enabled in production mode? What endpoints/schemas are exposed? Can it reveal internal API structure to attackers? Check enabledInProduction config.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Swagger UI properly disabled in production by default. Config::isEnabled() checks MODE_DEVELOPER || enabledInProduction (defaults false). No DI overrides found. REST schema endpoint exposure already covered by G-025. Host header in schema covered by L-063. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate CURL FTP protocol and arbitrary options SSRF amplification
archived_tasks.description: Framework CURL adapter enables FTP/FTPS protocols (CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS includes CURLPROTO_FTP). Client/Curl setOptions() accepts arbitrary curl options without validation. Trace all callers to check if any SSRF-exploitable endpoint uses FTP-enabled adapter.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated CURL FTP protocol and arbitrary options SSRF amplification. Both Framework CURL classes include FTP/FTPS in CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS by default. Adapter Curl setOptions accepts arbitrary CURLOPT_ constants. However: all callers pass hardcoded values, AllowedProtocols validator blocks FTP on RetrieveImage, no user-controllable setOptions path found. FTP amplification already in G-003. No new finding.

archived_tasks.title: Map PHP __destruct/__wakeup gadget chain surface for deserialization attacks
archived_tasks.description: IndexerTableSwapper::__destruct() can drop tables if $temporaryTables is controlled. Authorization/Role::__wakeup() gets ObjectManager. Config/Backend/Encrypted::__wakeup() restores encryptor. Map the full gadget chain surface and assess if any unserialize path could instantiate these objects (bypassing allowed_classes=false).
archived_tasks.result_summary: Mapped full PHP gadget chain surface for deserialization attacks. Found 29 __destruct and 28+ __wakeup methods. Application-level unserialize() consistently uses allowed_classes=false (Serialize.php:45), blocking object instantiation. phar:// stream wrapper explicitly disabled in app/bootstrap.php:12, closing the main bypass vector. The only viable gadget chain entry point is PHP session deserialization (G-011) which uses native unserialize() without allowed_classes. Key dangerous gadgets: IndexerTableSwapper::__destruct (DROP TABLE), Deploy/Queue::__destruct (kill PIDs), Archive/File::__destruct (file ops), Pdo/Mysql::__destruct (rollback). These are only reachable via G-011's Redis-based session injection. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate JWT token implementation security
archived_tasks.description: (task_072 completed core JWT; this covers Integration JWT + CardinalCommerce - reduced priority) Deep-dive into Magento JWT implementation: (1) Check web-token/jwt-framework 4 config for algorithm enforcement - is alg:none accepted? (2) Verify JWT secret/key management and rotation. (3) Check token expiration enforcement - admin 4hr, customer 1hr per config. (4) Verify JwtManagement.php (CardinalCommerce) signature validation is sound. (5) Check if opaque tokens vs JWT can be mixed to bypass validation. Files: Integration/Model/*, Integration/Api/TokenManager.php, CardinalCommerce/Model/JwtManagement.php NOTE: Overlaps with task_072 (tech_specific:jwt_security). task_072 covers core JWT framework; this covers Integration JWT + CardinalCommerce. One agent should reference the other.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated JWT implementation security across CardinalCommerce (custom JWT) and Integration/JwtUserToken (framework JWT). CardinalCommerce JwtManagement correctly enforces HS256 algorithm (blocks alg:none), uses timing-safe comparison (Security::compareStrings), and stores API keys encrypted. Framework JWT via ConfigurableJwtSettingsProvider only returns JWS/JWE settings, making NoEncryption/unsecured path unreachable for user tokens. CompositeTokenReader handles opaque-vs-JWT without confusion. All existing JWT findings (L-016, G-013) from task_072 confirmed as complete. No new vulnerabilities found.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate admin auth timing-based user enumeration
archived_tasks.description: Admin auth in User/Model/User.php:587 loads user by username first (loadByUsername), then only calls verifyIdentity (which runs Argon2 hash) if user exists. For non-existent users, no hash computation occurs - creating a timing difference. (1) Measure theoretical timing delta between existing vs non-existing admin users. (2) Check if RequestThrottler masks this at API level. (3) Check if admin lockout messages differentiate existing vs non-existing admin accounts. (4) Verify case-insensitive login (config flag use_case_sensitive_login) does not create additional enumeration via case normalization.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated all 4 aspects of admin auth timing enumeration. (1) Timing delta already confirmed in L-031. (2) RequestThrottler does NOT mask timing. (3) Lockout messages covered by G-006; three-band timing oracle confirmed. (4) Case-sensitive login (non-default) creates case-enumeration oracle. Updated L-031 with all findings. No new findings needed.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate session validation and fixation weaknesses
archived_tasks.description: Session validation is disabled by default (Store/etc/config.xml) - no IP/UA binding. Investigate: (1) Whether session ID in URL (SID) can be abused even though use_frontend_sid=0 by default. (2) LoginAsCustomer session handling - does admin impersonation properly isolate sessions? (3) Session cookie scope - can cross-store session hijacking occur in multi-store setups? (4) Admin session max size 256KB - what happens on overflow? (5) Verify session regeneration occurs on all privilege escalation points (login, checkout, admin login). (6) Check Persistent module for shopping cart persistence session issues.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated session validation weaknesses. Found G-033 (session max size write bypass). Session regeneration proper at all privilege escalation points. LoginAsCustomer isolates sessions correctly. SID deprecated. Persistent module disabled by default.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate @noEscape patterns for stored XSS via product attributes
archived_tasks.description: [DEMOTED meta7: subsumed by task_106/task_093] Catalog attribute.phtml uses @noEscape for product attribute values (line 53). Output::productAttribute() only escapes when is_html_allowed_on_front=false. Check which default attributes are HTML-allowed, whether customers can set these values via any path, and whether the MaliciousCode filter gap on WYSIWYG content is exploitable.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated @noEscape patterns with productAttribute() for stored XSS. No new finding - architecture is secure by design. productAttribute() conditionally escapes: non-HTML attributes get escapeHtml(), HTML-allowed attributes (description, short_description) are admin-only WYSIWYG fields. No customer path can inject HTML. Already covered by G-009 and G-021.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Elasticsearch query injection via search terms
archived_tasks.description: Wildcard filter wraps values with * without escaping (Wildcard.php:43). Check for query_string/simple_query_string usage, ValueTransformerPool sanitization, ES script queries, and whether search can enumerate private data.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated Elasticsearch query injection attack surface. No new findings beyond existing L-056 (wildcard metacharacter DoS in Advanced Search SKU). Regular search uses safe match/match_phrase queries. No query_string/simple_query_string usage. Painless scripts hardcoded with parameterized values. All queries sent as PHP arrays (JSON-serialized), preventing structural injection. Visibility filters prevent private data enumeration.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate IDOR in GraphQL resolvers accessing customer data
archived_tasks.description: (SUBSUMED by task_094) Check all GraphQL resolvers that accept customer_id, entity_id, or order_id as input. Verify they properly check ownership via getIsCustomer() context. Focus on: CustomerGraphQl, WishlistGraphQl, OrderGraphQl resolvers. Check if cart masked_quote_id is sufficiently unpredictable. NOTE: Overlaps with task_094 (graphql_idor_systematic). Whoever runs first should cover both scopes. Remaining task can verify gaps. [SUBSUMED by completed task_094]
archived_tasks.result_summary: Verification pass on GraphQL resolver IDOR coverage. Task was subsumed by completed task_094. Verified gap coverage across 40+ GraphQL modules. All customer-data resolvers properly validate ownership. No new findings - existing coverage is comprehensive.

archived_tasks.title: Verify stored XSS via API: trace customer name rendering
archived_tasks.description: [DEMOTED meta7: subsumed by task_106/task_093] M-010 found REST API XSS filter only blocks script tags. Trace where customer firstname/lastname, product names, and review text (settable via anonymous API) are rendered in admin HTML. Check if output encoding (htmlspecialchars/escapeHtml) is consistently applied. If any path lacks encoding, this becomes high-severity stored XSS.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated stored XSS via API rendering paths. Customer firstname/lastname, product names, review text, gift messages, and order comments are all consistently escaped with escapeHtml() in admin templates. Address JSON in order-create script tags is protected by PHP json_encode default forward-slash escaping (prevents script breakout). Email template directives default to escape modifier. M-010 weak script-only XSS filter is defense-in-depth only - output encoding provides robust protection. No new stored XSS findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate REST API mass assignment via ServiceInputProcessor
archived_tasks.description: [DEMOTED meta7: subsumed by task_106/task_093] (OVERLAP with task_093 - cover ServiceInputProcessor scope) ServiceInputProcessor._createFromArray() auto-invokes setter methods for any matching property name. Check: Can custom_attributes set internal attributes? Can extension_attributes be abused on anon endpoints? Are there sensitive setters on Customer/Quote interfaces? Focus on /V1/customers (anon POST) and /V1/guest-carts.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed mass assignment via POST /V1/customers (anonymous registration). group_id can be set to any valid customer group (Wholesale, Retailer, custom). Filed M-031.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate injection via search criteria filters
archived_tasks.description: REST SearchCriteria and GraphQL product search accept filter field names and condition types from user input. Check: Are filter field names validated? Can conditionType lead to SQL injection? Is anonymous /V1/search exploitable? How are Elasticsearch queries built from user input?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated SearchCriteria filter injection surface. SQL injection via conditionType/field is prevented by parameterized queries (quoteInto) and field name quoting (quoteIdentifier). However, the regexp condition type exposes MySQL REGEXP to user-controlled patterns on anonymous endpoints including /V1/products-render-info. MySQL 8.0+ uses ICU backtracking regex, making ReDoS possible. Recorded as L-067. Elasticsearch wildcard injection was already covered by L-056. No field name allowlisting at API layer, but EAV collections validate attributes exist.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate addData/setData mass assignment patterns in admin controllers
archived_tasks.description: Variable/Validate.php uses addData($this->getRequest()->getPost(variable)) without allowlist. Search for similar patterns across all admin controllers where POST data is passed directly to model addData/setData/create. Check if any allow setting sensitive fields (is_active, role_id, etc). Grep for addData($this->getRequest, setData($this->getRequest, ->create($this->getRequest patterns in Controller/Adminhtml.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated addData/setData mass assignment patterns across admin controllers. Found 20+ controllers with the pattern, all admin-only with ACL. Updated G-023 to reflect broader scope. No new findings - pattern is architectural choice within admin trust boundary. Critical mass assignment (unauthenticated REST API) already covered by M-031.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate private_content_version cookie cache poisoning potential
archived_tasks.description: L-010: PageCache Version cookie uses md5(rand().time()) and HttpOnly=false. Investigate: (1) How does Varnish/PageCache use this cookie value? (2) Can a predictable cookie value enable cache key differential attacks? (3) Is the cookie used in any security-sensitive context beyond cache busting? (4) Can XSS read+replay this cookie to force cache invalidation for other users?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated private_content_version cookie for cache poisoning potential. Confirmed it is NOT used in Varnish cache keying (Varnish uses X-Magento-Vary for hash_data). The cookie is purely a client-side version indicator that triggers JS AJAX refetch of private content sections. HttpOnly=false is intentional (JS must read it). Cookie value is not a secret and predictability has no security impact. L-010 remains correctly classified as low/defense-in-depth. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Admin SecretKey MD5-based HMAC and potential forgery
archived_tasks.description: Admin SecretKey = HMAC(route+controller+action+formKey, crypt_key). Investigate: (1) If formKey is leaked (XSS/logging), can attacker compute valid secret keys? (2) The getHash function uses HMAC-SHA256 by default which is good, but check if MD5 version can be forced. (3) Is the secretKey compared timing-safely at BackendValidator:111? (confirmed ===) (4) Can secretKey be leaked via Referer header on admin links?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated Admin SecretKey HMAC mechanism. SecretKey uses HMAC-SHA256 (not MD5) with crypt/key - MD5 cannot be forced. FormKey leak alone insufficient without crypt/key. BackendValidator fallback path uses non-timing-safe === comparison but is only reached for non-AbstractAction controllers (extremely rare). No Referrer-Policy header set but secret keys are route-specific and session-bound. Recorded G-034 (informational) for the === inconsistency.

archived_tasks.title: Verify REST API email change bypass and check other sensitive field changes
archived_tasks.description: (SUBSUMED by task_133) M-013: PUT /V1/customers/me allows email change without re-auth. Investigate: (1) Confirm email change works without password via REST. (2) Check if other sensitive fields can be modified. (3) Check notification emails. (4) Check for plugins adding re-auth. (5) Check SOAP equivalent. [SUBSUMED by completed task_133]
archived_tasks.result_summary: Task subsumed by completed task_133. All investigation items covered by existing findings: M-013, H-005, M-026, L-025, M-021. SOAP uses same interface. Email notification exists but is post-save, not prevention. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Order state machine transition validation audit
archived_tasks.description: Order.setState() has no transition validation. Investigate: (1) Code paths calling setState bypassing can* checks. (2) Order status manipulation via REST comments API. (3) Race conditions between concurrent state changes. (4) Cancel/uncancel abuse. (5) forced_can_creditmemo flag abuse.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated order state machine transition validation. Order::setState() is a bare data setter with no transition validation. REST API endpoints allow admin users to set arbitrary order states bypassing business logic checks. Filed L-068.

archived_tasks.title: Credit memo and refund business logic abuse investigation
archived_tasks.description: Investigate refund/credit memo abuse: (1) totalRefunded exceeding totalPaid via float manipulation. (2) adjustment_negative abuse. (3) Race conditions between concurrent credit memos. (4) Partial refund chaining. (5) Admin REST API refund IDOR.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated credit memo/refund business logic abuse across 5 dimensions. (1) Float precision: properly handled via priceCurrency->round(). (2) Negative adjustments: L-048 updated with shipping_amount negative vector. (3) Race conditions: M-020 confirmed. (4) Partial refund chaining: properly validated via QuantityValidator. (5) Admin REST API IDOR: all endpoints admin-only ACL.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate OrderMutex coverage gap: hold/unHold/addComment race conditions
archived_tasks.description: (OVERLAP with task_119 - focus on OrderMutex hold/unHold/addComment specifically) M-015: OrderService hold/unHold/addComment lack OrderMutex while cancel/refund/invoice/ship use it. Verify: (1) Can hold+cancel race corrupt order state? (2) Can addComment change status while cancel is executing? (3) Are there REST/GraphQL endpoints that expose hold/unHold to non-admin users? (4) Check if CreditmemoService.refund() (using its own beginTransaction but not OrderMutex) can race with cancel(). (5) Check webapi.xml for hold/unhold endpoints.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Verified M-015 finding: OrderService::hold(), unHold(), and addComment() confirmed to lack OrderMutex while cancel/invoice/refund/ship use it. All three endpoints are admin-only REST API (Magento_Sales::hold, ::unhold, ::comment ACL). No GraphQL exposure. Race window confirmed: hold() loads order without lock, cancel() acquires SELECT FOR UPDATE via OrderMutex. If hold() loads before cancel() commits, hold() overwrites canceled state. addComment() can similarly overwrite state changes from mutex-protected operations. OrderRepository::save() has no optimistic locking to prevent stale writes. No new findings — M-015 accurately covers this issue.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate admin audit logging completeness
archived_tasks.description: No AdminLogger/ActionLog module found in CE. Only event-based observers for config changes. Investigate: (1) Are admin login/logout events logged to persistent storage? (2) Are order state changes (cancel, refund, status change) logged with admin user ID? (3) Are customer data exports/views logged? (4) Are ACL/role changes logged? (5) Is there any mechanism to detect insider abuse (LoginAsCustomer, mass data export)? This is an OWASP A09:2025 check.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated admin audit logging completeness. Found systematic gaps: sales_order_status_history has no user_id (unlike shipment/invoice/creditmemo comments), no persistent admin login log, no config change audit trail, no data export logging, no ACL/role change logging. LoginAsCustomer has partial logging (login only, not actions or logout). Recorded as L-069.

archived_tasks.title: Check jQuery $.extend usage for prototype pollution in Magento UI components
archived_tasks.description: Magento heavily uses jQuery and RequireJS. Check if jQuery.extend(true, ...) is called with user-controlled input. Also check for custom merge/deepExtend patterns in Magento UI lib. jQuery 3.x protects against __proto__ in $.extend, but check the exact jQuery version used and whether custom merge utilities exist. Also check for prototype pollution gadgets in KO component initialization.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated jQuery extend and custom merge patterns for prototype pollution. jQuery 3.7.1 blocks __proto__ in extend. However, setNested in mage/utils/objects.js lacks __proto__ sanitization and is confirmed vulnerable to prototype pollution via path traversal. No current code path routes user-controlled dot-separated keys to the vulnerable function. Recorded as informational gadget (G-035) that chains with KO html: binding gadgets (G-009).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate rule condition dynamic class instantiation from admin request params
archived_tasks.description: CatalogRule/SalesRule NewConditionHtml controllers accept 'type' param from request and instantiate the class via ObjectManager::create(). While admin-only and restricted to ConditionInterface, verify: (1) Can the interface check be bypassed? (2) What classes implement ConditionInterface - any with dangerous constructors? (3) Are there any non-admin callers of ConditionFactory::create()? (4) Can the type parameter include namespace traversal?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated NewConditionHtml and NewActionHtml admin controllers for arbitrary class instantiation. Found NewActionHtml controllers (SalesRule + CatalogRule) have NO pre-instantiation type check. Recorded as L-070 (low, admin-only).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Curl adapter protocol override via setOptions/addOption
archived_tasks.description: Framework/HTTP/Adapter/Curl.php accepts arbitrary CURLOPT_* integer keys via setOptions(). Callers can override CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS to allow additional protocols (file://, gopher://). Framework/HTTP/Client/Curl.php also allows FTP/FTPS by default. Investigate: (1) Which callers use addOption/setOptions with user-influenced values? (2) Can PayPal/shipping carrier setOptions calls be influenced? (3) Is _config merge order exploitable (caller options override defaults)? Also check if any caller can override CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated Curl adapter setOptions/addOption protocol override potential. No user-controlled data reaches setOptions/addOption on either Curl adapter. TransferBuilder.setClientConfig() never called. No CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION override. All callers pass hardcoded or admin-configured values. FTP/FTPS default already covered by G-003/G-004. No new finding.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate Downloadable product get_headers() redirect chain for SSRF bypass
archived_tasks.description: Downloadable/Helper/Download.php:266 uses get_headers() which follows redirects. An admin-set URL could redirect to internal network. The Sample download is unauthenticated. Investigate: (1) Can admin set sample URL via REST API? (2) Does get_headers() follow multiple redirect hops? (3) After redirect, does fileGetContents/fopen fetch the final URL (internal)? (4) Is response content returned to the requesting user (full vs blind SSRF)? (5) Can the redirect target be file:// or other protocols?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated downloadable product get_headers() redirect SSRF chain. Confirmed full read SSRF via redirect: admin sets whitelisted domain URL, domain redirects to internal IP, get_headers() follows redirect, _getHandle() connects to internal target, output() streams response to unauthenticated requester. DomainValidator only validates initial URL at REST API save time, not redirect targets. Admin UI save path has no domain validation at all. Updated G-010 with complete technical chain. No new findings - existing G-004 and G-010 cover this.

archived_tasks.title: Coupon double-use race condition: verify no forensic trail (CC1 compound)
archived_tasks.description: M-014 found TOCTOU in coupon per-customer usage. CC1 compound pattern asks: if attacker exploits the race to use a coupon twice, is there any audit log recording the anomaly? Check: 1) Does coupon usage update create any log entry? 2) Can the double-use be detected forensically after the fact? 3) Is there a reconciliation cron? 4) What is the maximum financial impact?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed no audit trail for coupon double-use race (M-014). Usage update pipeline has zero logging, no reconciliation cron (daily cron only aggregates reports), and counter drift from lost updates is permanent. Forensic detection possible via manual SQL but not automated. Recorded as L-071.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate full scope of checkout window.checkoutConfig data exposure
archived_tasks.description: DefaultConfigProvider::getQuoteData() uses $quote->toArray() exposing all quote DB columns to frontend JS. Investigate: (1) What exact fields are exposed (remote_ip confirmed, check password_hash population), (2) Check all ConfigProviderInterface implementations for similar over-exposure, (3) Check if reserved_order_id is predictable for order ID enumeration, (4) Check if any CompositeConfigProvider implementations leak API keys or internal state. Related finding: L-020.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated full scope of checkout window.checkoutConfig data exposure. Validated L-020 (quote-level toArray overexposure). Discovered L-072: getQuoteItemData() also uses unfiltered toArray(), exposing base_cost (wholesale cost price) as business-sensitive data. Reviewed all 24 ConfigProviderInterface implementations - none leak API keys or credentials.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate payment debug logging for sensitive data exposure
archived_tasks.description: Verify what data Payment/Gateway/Http/Client/Zend and Soap clients log when debug is enabled. Check all implementations of PaymentMethodLogger callers. Verify CardinalCommerce JWT logging masks sufficient claims (currently only masks iss). Check if shipping carrier debug logging (AbstractCarrier:611) logs customer PII. Related finding: L-021.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed L-021 (payment debug logging with empty mask keys). Added L-073: shipping carrier debug logging exposes customer PII without masking. FedEx only masks API credentials, DHL JSON filterDebugData silently fails on XML parser. CardinalCommerce JWT logging only masks iss claim.

archived_tasks.title: Verify InvoiceService setCapture/setVoid race impact on payment gateways
archived_tasks.description: L-022: InvoiceService::setCapture() and setVoid() (REST /V1/invoices/:id/capture and /V1/invoices/:id/void) lack OrderMutex. Investigate: (1) Can concurrent capture+void both succeed causing double payment gateway calls? (2) Does the payment gateway adapter have its own idempotency? (3) What is the worst-case financial impact of concurrent invoice operations? (4) Check Invoice::canCapture() and canVoid() guards under concurrency.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Validated L-022 (InvoiceService setCapture/setVoid missing OrderMutex). Confirmed race condition: concurrent requests both load same invoice, both pass isPaid TOCTOU check, both trigger gateway calls. Discovered new finding L-074: setVoid has no persistence plugin - gateway void fires but invoice/order state not saved to DB (functional correctness bug).

archived_tasks.title: Verify Cron trySetJobUniqueStatusAtomic variable shadowing bug impact
archived_tasks.description: Cron/Model/ResourceModel/Schedule.php:65 trySetJobUniqueStatusAtomic has variable shadowing: line 94 overwrites $scheduleId parameter with fetchOne result (NULL when no running job found), then line 105 uses this NULL value in UPDATE WHERE clause, matching no rows. The schedule never gets marked running. Appears unused in current code (only trySetJobStatusAtomic is called). Verify: (1) Is this function actually called anywhere? (2) If unused, is it dead code? (3) If called by extensions, could it cause cron double-execution?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed variable shadowing bug in trySetJobUniqueStatusAtomic (Schedule.php:94). Line 94 overwrites scheduleId parameter with fetchOne() result (NULL), causing the UPDATE on line 105 to match zero rows. Function always returns true but never marks schedule as running. Unused in core but marked @api @since 100.2.0. Extensions calling it get no mutual exclusion, enabling cron double-execution. Recorded as L-075 (low, confidence 0.95).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate locale-dependent number parsing edge cases in financial operations
archived_tasks.description: FormatInterface::getNumber() (Framework/Locale/Format.php:77) strips non-digit characters via regex and handles comma/dot based on locale. This is used across 20+ files for price/qty parsing. Investigate: (1) Can locale switching change how the same numeric string is parsed mid-session? (2) Arabic locale normalization path at line 88 - what transformations does normalizeArabicLocale apply? (3) Japan locale hardcode at line 112 - comma as thousands separator. (4) Negative numbers pass through the regex (hyphen preserved) - trace all callers to verify negative values are handled downstream. (5) getNumber returns null for null input (line 79-81) - check if any callers pass null and then do arithmetic on the result.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated locale-dependent number parsing in FormatInterface::getNumber(). Confirmed comma-grouped numbers like 1,000 silently misparsed as 1.0 for non-Japanese locales, affecting 30+ callers. Recorded L-076 (low severity - admin-only, requires locale mismatch).

archived_tasks.title: Investigate creditmemo adjustment percentage and negative value edge cases
archived_tasks.description: Creditmemo::setAdjustmentAmount() (Sales/Model/Order/Creditmemo.php:542-555) parses percentage values (ending with %) and computes amount from order GrandTotal. Investigate: (1) Can adjustment_positive with a very large percentage (e.g., 99999%) create a refund exceeding order value? The isValidGrandTotal check at line 665 rejects <=0 but not >orderTotal. (2) Can negative adjustment_positive (e.g., "-50") be used to reduce refund amount? (3) CreditmemoFactory::parseAdjustmentAmount passes through percentage sign - verify the Creditmemo::setAdjustmentAmount handles the percent parsing correctly after locale number parsing. (4) Check REST API creditmemo creation path for same edge cases - does webapi enforce stricter validation?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated creditmemo adjustment percentage and negative value edge cases. Large percentage values compute huge amounts but validateForRefund() in CreditmemoService rejects if baseTotalRefunded + baseGrandTotal > baseTotalPaid, preventing monetary over-refund. Negative adjustment_positive already covered by L-048. REST API paths protected by same validation. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate REST/GraphQL error message disclosure in developer mode
archived_tasks.description: Webapi/Rest/Request/Deserializer/Json.php:66-75 leaks stack traces in developer mode error responses. Verify: (1) Is developer mode detectable from outside? (2) What other error handlers in REST/GraphQL leak stack traces in developer mode? (3) Can error messages in production mode still leak sensitive info (DB table names, file paths)?
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated REST/GraphQL error disclosure. Developer mode stack trace exposure already covered by L-065. Found new production-mode issue: ErrorProcessor.processLocalizedException() passes raw exception messages unmasked to API clients. 33+ locations wrap database/internal exceptions into LocalizedException with $e->getMessage(), leaking DB schema info even in production. Guest-accessible endpoints affected. GraphQL better protected. Recorded as L-077.

archived_tasks.title: Check if admin account email/password change revokes other admin sessions and tokens
archived_tasks.description: The Backend\Controller\Adminhtml\System\Account\Save controller handles admin account changes. It requires performIdentityCheck (re-auth) but check if it invalidates other active admin sessions after email or password change. Verify if admin API tokens are revoked. Compare with the AdminUser plugin in Integration module.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Confirmed that admin password/email change via My Account (Account Save) does NOT invalidate other active admin sessions. The parallel ResetPasswordPost controller correctly calls ForceSignIn::updateAdminSessionStatus(). The admin-manages-admin Save controller also misses session invalidation. Recorded as L-078. Chains with existing L-064 (tokens not revoked on password change).

archived_tasks.title: Dynamic config (core_config_data) attack surface
archived_tasks.description: 501 config refs, 250 files, AsyncConfig MQ consumer. Investigate MQ config injection, encrypted readback, base URL manipulation, CSP weakening, config import/export, cache race.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated core_config_data attack surface. Found L-079: AsyncConfig MQ consumer bypasses admin ACL. Base URL validation properly implemented. Config values validated via backend models. No REST API for config. clone_fields groups bypass filterNodes (1 instance in Catalog).

archived_tasks.title: MQ consumer auth and message injection
archived_tasks.description: 12 consumers. Critical: saveConfigProcessor, MassConsumer, exportProcessor. Investigate MQ injection for config, MassConsumer auth, message serialization, RabbitMQ creds, export file ops.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated 12+ MQ consumers for injection/auth/message integrity. Found: L-080 (AMQP no TLS default), G-036 (no message-level auth on any consumer). Export filename safe. L-079 already covers AsyncConfig. MassConsumer isSecureArea=true globally.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate CMS WYSIWYG media storage upload and directory operations
archived_tasks.description: CMS WYSIWYG Images Storage (Cms/Model/Wysiwyg/Images/Storage.php) handles file upload, directory creation/deletion. Check: (1) isDirectoryAllowed() bypass via path manipulation, (2) getAllowedPathPattern() regex bypass, (3) uploadFile targetPath traversal, (4) createDirectory name injection, (5) deleteFile/deleteDirectory traversal. Admin-only but high-impact if bypassed.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated CMS WYSIWYG Images Storage for path traversal, directory bypass, and upload security. All five concerns analyzed. Defenses are layered and effective: isDirectoryAllowed() uses strict regex [a-zA-Z0-9-_], getRealPathSafety resolves .., PathValidator checks containment. All controllers admin-only with Magento_Cms::media_gallery ACL. No exploitable vulnerabilities found.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate import/export file handling for path traversal and injection
archived_tasks.description: ImportExport module handles CSV file uploads and processing. Check: (1) uploadFileAndGetSource() file handling, (2) CSV injection in imported data (fputcsv), (3) Import file stored in var/importexport - check path construction, (4) MediaStorage Uploader renameFile entity parameter is user-influenced. The import functionality processes CSV that could contain formulas.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated import/export file handling. Entity parameter in renameFile() is validated against whitelist - no path traversal. Export file Delete controller path traversal already covered by G-019. Import image SSRF already covered by M-004. Updated M-002 with corrected technical details (sanitization DOES exist for =,+,- but missing @). Discovered AwsS3 driver polymorphic gap - filePutCsv() lacks all formula sanitization present in File driver (L-081). History download uses basename() safely.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate CSV formula injection in export module
archived_tasks.description: CSV export at ImportExport/Model/Export/Adapter/Csv.php:141 writes user-controlled data without formula sanitization. Trace all export paths (product, customer, order, review, tax rates). Verify which user-controlled fields reach CSV output. Check if any sanitization exists in export model before writeRow. Confirm unauthenticated injection vectors (customer registration, product reviews).
archived_tasks.result_summary: Validated M-002 CSV formula injection finding. Confirmed: (1) @ character missing from sanitization list in File.php:876 and Io/File.php:201, (2) AwsS3 driver completely bypasses all sanitization (L-081), (3) Tab and CR characters also bypass. Input validation blocks formula chars in most customer fields, but company address field has NO validator. Finding confirmed at medium severity.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate all callers of Filesystem/Driver/Http for SSRF paths
archived_tasks.description: The HTTP filesystem driver (file_get_contents, fsockopen) has no SSRF protection. Investigate all callers beyond import: ReadFactory usage, any code path where user input can reach the HTTP driver. Check if REST/GraphQL API can trigger product import remotely.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated all callers of Filesystem/Driver/Http for SSRF paths. Found exactly two code paths to the HTTP driver: (1) CatalogImportExport/Model/Import/Uploader::downloadFileFromUrl() - admin-only import, already covered by M-004; (2) Downloadable/Helper/Download::_getHandle() and setResource() - admin-created URLs triggered by customer/anonymous downloads, already covered by G-004/G-010. No REST API or GraphQL endpoints expose import functionality. All ReadFactory->create() calls outside these two paths use DriverPool::FILE. No additional SSRF paths discovered.

archived_tasks.title: Investigate shipping carrier config URL injection for SSRF
archived_tasks.description: UPS, DHL, USPS, FedEx carriers use config-based URLs for API calls. UPS validates ups.com domain. Check: (1) Can admin override gateway URLs? (2) Do other carriers validate domains? (3) Can carrier URL config values be injected to target internal services? (4) StompClient Jolokia host from deployment config - verify it cannot be set from admin panel.
archived_tasks.result_summary: Investigated shipping carrier config URL injection for SSRF. UPS, USPS, and FedEx all have domain-validating backend models restricting URLs to their respective carrier domains. DHL URLs are NOT admin-configurable. No new findings.

archived_tasks.title: JWT token replay: no binding to IP/client/session
archived_tasks.description: JWT user tokens have no fingerprint binding (IP, User-Agent, etc). Investigate: 1) Can a stolen JWT be replayed from different IP/client? 2) Is there any session binding or device fingerprinting? 3) Are tokens invalidated on password change? 4) Is the revocation mechanism (RevokedValidator) triggered on password change and admin lockout? Check Integration/Plugin/Model/AdminUser.php and CustomerUser.php for revocation on user state changes.
archived_tasks.result_summary: JWT token replay investigation complete. JWT tokens contain only uid, utypid, iat, exp - no IP/UA/session fingerprint binding. Standard bearer token behavior (RFC 6750). Validator chain (ExpirationValidator + RevokedValidator) has no client-binding checks. Admin lockout uses direct SQL bypassing ORM so tokens not revoked during lockout. All substantive issues already covered by M-021, L-064, L-045, G-013, L-016, L-032. No new finding warranted.
